item.title: Two pilots dead after Air Canada Express jet collides with firefighting vehicle at LaGuardia : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: Two pilots are dead and at least 41 others were taken to hospital after an Air Canada Express flight collided with a Port Authority aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicle while landing at New York’s LaGuardia Airport late Sunday, officials said Monday.

item.title: Marking World Tuberculosis Day : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: Today (Tues.) is World Tuberculosis Day, and Northeastern Public Health is joining the global movement to make people aware of it and work towards getting rid of it.

item.title: Former bowling alley demolished after roof collapse in Kap : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: Demolition is underway on the former bowling alley after the roof collapsed yesterday morning in Kapuskasing.

item.title: Progress report on veterinary services for Kap expected at meeting next month : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: Progress that a veterinary recruitment committee is making to bring a vet to Kapuskasing will be discussed during an important meeting on Tuesday, April 14th at 6 pm at the Civic Centre.

item.title: District hospital names new CEO : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: There’s a new president and CEO moving into the office at the Timmins and District Hospital on June 1st.

item.title: Kap fire chief says be mindful to check snow on roofs of homes and businesses : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: In the wake of two roof collapses in four days... The Kapuskasing fire chief admits that two major snowstorms in November and December prompted him to get firefighters to check on roofs of home and businesses.

item.title: Malette promotes Hwy. 11 safety in House of Commons : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: Another call in the House of Commons concerning the safety of Northern Ontario highways.

item.title: Kap Gives Back hockey tourney and fundraiser ready for Easter weekend : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: The end of hockey season will be punctuated in a big way on Easter weekend with the Kap Gives Back hockey tourney and fundraiser at the Sports Palace.

item.title: FONOM likes what it sees in several Ontario budget measures : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: The Federation of Northern Ontario Municipalities (FONOM) says several measures in the provincial budget will support communities, economic growth, and quality of life across Northern Ontario.

item.title: Construction of new seniors apartment complex in Smooth Rock Falls to start this summer : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: A consultant with a group bringing a seniors housing complex to Smooth Rock Falls says design stage is underway, and he is hopeful to have shovels in the ground by this summer.

item.title: Sports dome construction begins at Northern College : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: The ground has been officially broken for the new sports dome on the Northern College Timmins campus.

item.title: Moose Factory man wins TADHF 50-50 : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: A Moose Factory man is the winner of the March 50-50 draw by the Timmins and District Hospital Foundation.

item.title: Back to school for Nouveau Regard : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: It’s back to school for some students of Ecole Catholique Nouveau Regard in Cochrane this week.

item.title: Preloved Shop wins Hearst business of the year award : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: The Preloved Shop was shown a lot of love and chosen as the big winner of Business of the Year during the Prix Panache Hearst Business Awards on Saturday night.

item.title: Kap History - Bowling alley first opened in 1959 : My Kap-Hearst Now
item.description: This week’s look at Kapuskasing history explores the past behind the old bowling alley on Byng Avenue following the roof collapse and demolition of the building last week.
